text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Monday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The prosecutor's office is continuing its investigation into former central bank chief Kazys Ratkevichius and the head of the Soviet Vneshekonombank branch in Lithuania Danute Tuchkiene.
- Discus thrower Virgilijus Alekna, 25, won the silver medal in the world athletics championship in Athens. Alekna is a bodyguard to President Algirdas Brazauskas.
- The low exchange rate of the German mark hit Lithuanian companies which export to Germany.
- The 10 leading breweries produced 17.21 million litres of beer in July, six million litres more than in the same period in 1996.
- The supervisors' board of Mazheikiu Nafta oil refinery approved the firm's 18.2 million litas profit for the first half of 1997.
- Inflation in Lithuania was 1.1 percent in July and was the highest among the three Baltic countries.
- The second privatisation tender for State Commercial Bank failed to attract investor's attention again. Potential buyers said the privatisation terms were not concrete enough.
- 20 state-run enterprises will be offered on open auction at the stock exchange Monday. Three of them are expected to be sold.
- Only 500 agricultural co-operatives out of a registered 2,000 registered operate on the market and more than 1,000 are on the verge of bankruptcy.
- The Ekspres Taxi company, which won exclusive rights to serve Vilnius airport, has cut the number of illegal taxi drivers at the airport, which are known to cheat clients.
- Vilniaus Tauras brewery posted a 1.535 million litas net profit for the first half of 1997.
- Kraft Jacobs Suchard Lietuva said it sold 7,015 tonnes of its products in the first half of the year compared to 6,998 tonnes in the same period in 1996.
